statement.text:
A family F of group homomorphisms A → B is separating if for every
nontrivial a ∈ A there is f ∈ F such that f (a) ̸= 1, and discriminating if for any
finitely many nontrivial elements a1 , . . . , an ∈ A there is f ∈ F such that f (ai ) ̸= 1 for
all i = 1, . . . , n. Let G be a relatively free group of rank 2 in the variety of metabelian
groups. Let T be a metabelian group in which the centralizer of every nontrivial
element is abelian. If T admits a separating family of surjective homomorphisms
T → G must it also admit a discriminating family of surjective homomorphisms
T → G?
    A positive answer would give a metabelian analogue of a classical theorem of
B. Baumslag.                                                        A. Gaglione, D. Spellman
